# Lab 14.5: AI.SIMILARITY

## What We Are Going to Do
Compare two inputs by meaning with AI.SIMILARITY, with no stored embeddings.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Compare word pairs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  AI.SIMILARITY('happy', 'glad', endpoint =&gt; 'text-embedding-005') AS synonyms,
  AI.SIMILARITY('happy', 'invoice', endpoint =&gt; 'text-embedding-005') AS unrelated,
  AI.SIMILARITY('How to bake a cake', 'Recipes for desserts', model =&gt; 'embeddinggemma-300m') AS related;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Find the closest articles.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT title,
  AI.SIMILARITY('housing market downward trends', body, endpoint =&gt; 'text-embedding-005') AS score
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 5;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Find duplicate questions.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT a.title AS q1, b.title AS q2,
  AI.SIMILARITY(a.title, b.title, model =&gt; 'embeddinggemma-300m') AS score
FROM (SELECT * FROM lab14.so_questions LIMIT 30) a
JOIN (SELECT * FROM lab14.so_questions LIMIT 30) b ON a.id &lt; b.id
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 5;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **When to use what.** AI.SIMILARITY is best for a small number of comparisons. For many searches over a large table, store embeddings and use VECTOR_SEARCH or AI.SEARCH.

5. **[CLI] Compare two words from bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
"SELECT AI.SIMILARITY('car', 'automobile', model =&gt; 'embeddinggemma-300m') AS close, AI.SIMILARITY('car', 'banana', model =&gt; 'embeddinggemma-300m') AS far"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Output | Cosine similarity, close to 1 = similar |
| Synonyms | Around 0.9 |
| Unrelated words | Much lower |
| Scale | Small comparisons only |
